Both done before the r3 run. Fresh held-out set, written after the r2 fixes and labelled before it was run. Not used to tune. Labels are a designer's call, not the code's rule: shouldAsk is true when the request fits a part and a designer would ask before building (two shapes named, a nav with no platform, a data view with no state named). Buttons, CTAs, fields and state parts are labelled no-ask. expect is the part a designer means, or null when nothing in the Acme library fits. Part recall: fitting requests where brief offered expect (candidate, option, or candidate after the first option of each question). Part precision: requests where brief offered parts and expect was among them. Question recall and precision use shouldAsk. The numbers below are what the test measured; the test fails if they move. First run: question recall 9/12, precision 9/14; it found one bug (an approved decision matched on the part's own plural, so data tables of payments skipped as a decision), fixed before these numbers. Misses left: a nav bar for the app and top nav for the payees get no part because recommend finds none with the extra words (recommend recall, PR #59); fields, CTAs and buttons get a states question a designer would skip. r3 run: question recall 7/9, precision 7/8, 0.16 questions per request, max 1; misses are the two navs (recommend finds no part) and save ctas (asked states; labelled no-ask). r4 run: question recall 4/6, precision 4/5, 0.09 questions per request, max 1, part recall 33/35; same three misses. Merged with PR #59 and PR #68 (recommend recall + general matching): recommend now finds the two navs, so question recall 6/6, precision 6/7, part recall 35/35, 0.13 questions per request, max 1; save ctas is still asked states (labelled no-ask).
